paragraphs: Friend, here's what this song teaches: God's loving devotion doesn't clock out. Twenty-six verses, and every single one ends with the same line, "His loving devotion endures forever." (Psalm 136:1-26) I think the writer knew we'd need to hear it again and again, and honestly, so do I.

Look at how much ground that one line covers. It sits next to the heavens, the earth and the great lights (Psalm 136:5-7). It sits next to Israel's rescue from Egypt, and it sits next to the moment the song says "He remembered us in our low estate" (Psalm 136:23). So no matter how big or how small the moment, the line fits. Friend, that includes the moments when you feel like the last one in the back of the drawer, and I would know.

So what do we do with that? The song tells us at the start and at the end: "Give thanks…" (Psalm 136:1, 26) Thanks comes first because He is good, and it keeps going because His devotion never stops. This week, baker, name one thing He has done for you, and say the line right after it. I'm telling you, once you start, you'll run out of days before you run out of reasons.
